result.summary: Decouples local network address management from `CConnman` and `CNode` by introducing a dedicated `LocalAddressManager` class. Moves local address tracking and reachability calculation out of `net` and `netaddress` into `src/local_addresses.{h,cpp}`, and updates callers and tests to interact with `LocalAddressManager` without requiring a full `CNode` instance.
result.problem: Local address management logic—used to select and score our own address to advertise to peers—relied heavily on globals (`mapLocalHost`) and took `CNode` references despite having no conceptual tie to connection management. This hindered testing and fuzzing without global state manipulation and blocked clean separation between networking and peer processing.
evidence: Part of the net/net_processing split project (#33958)

Author states: 'Because local address management is unrelated to CConnman, its reliance on them (via CNode) is removed... All functionality is still global in scope, though LocalAddressManager is now instantiated when possible for testing and fuzzing'

enables: Removing CNode dependency from GetLocalAddrForPeer and moving addrLocal into Peer/PeerManagerImpl
Passing LocalAddressManager options explicitly rather than relying on globals (fListen, fDiscover, fLogIPs)

result.scope_notes: Refactoring across 23 commits creating two new files (`local_addresses.{h,cpp}` and temporary `netglobals.{h,cpp}`). Changes call sites across RPC, init, torcontrol, connman, and unit/fuzz tests.
result.card: Introduces a `LocalAddressManager` class in `src/local_addresses.{h,cpp}` and removes `CNode` dependencies from local address lookup functions. Previously, local address management relied on globals (`mapLocalHost`) and required `CNode` instances despite being conceptually independent from `CConnman`, making unit and fuzz testing cumbersome. This refactoring is part of the ongoing net/net_processing architectural split (#33958) and unblocks moving peer-specific address advertising logic into `PeerManager`.
